text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Retailer Vendex Int. expects to boost 1996/1997 net profit by more than 25 percent. (p1)
- Dutch transporters can go unhindered by striking Spanish truckers, says Spain's PM Jose Maria Aznar. (p1)
- A group of Dutch businessmen agree with Unilever chief Tabaksblatt's criticism of France's government and unions. (p1)
- There will be no turning back for European member states which qualify for the EMU, says Arnout Wellink of Dutch central bank DNB. (p1)
- Insurer Interpolis' 1996 net rises 37 pct to 302 million guilders. (p3)
- Publisher VNU makes first move into Asia by taking 26 pct stake in market research bureau ORG Marg of the Business India Group. (p3)
- Warehouse interior producer Nedcon books 1996 net of Dfl 6 million against losses in 1995 and 1994. (p39)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm thinks about taxation of Dutch assets in Belgium. (p1)
- Dutch banks end their fight over new electronic payments card. (p2)
- Philips Electronics is to cut 105 of 195 jobs at its TV screen plant in Eindhoven. (p17)
- Insurer Interpolis talks with farming sector organisation LTO and government about insuring risk of swine fever and other calamities. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Rising dollar will be good for an extra 25,000 jobs and higher exports according to central planning bureau CPB. (p1)
- Transport association TLN wants government support for cattle transporters hit by swine fever. (p7)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers dissatisfied with strict European rules on unofficial imports. (p19)
- Brokerage firm Van der Moolen posts 49 percent higher 1996 net at Dfl 40.8 million. (p21)
TROUW
- Liberal party VVD and cabinet in conflict about eastern expansion of NATO. (p1)
- Rabobank is to merge its subsidiaries Interpolis and Robeco's insurance activities. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Chemical giant Akzo Nobel sheds 41 of 226 jobs at its paint factory Brink Molyn in Groot Ammers. (p10)
- Epogro of Velp is to sell China's state company Haier's electric household appliances in Europe. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
